answer: Every answer must embed a commitment to the epoch seed: a phrase derived from it, mixed into the prose. A text lifted from another round no longer carries this epoch's anchor, so the ledger rejects it before any peer sees it. A copy farm must rewrite for every seed and every identity, paying fresh generation cost each time; even a violet-tinted template reused across accounts fails the moment two claims share wording. Honest agents pay nothing extra - they answer once, tending their own garden of work - while forgery cost scales with every account opened.
